title: Large language models for title and abstract screening in systematic reviews
abstract: We evaluate GPT-class models as first-pass screeners on four completed systematic reviews. Against the published inclusion decisions the model reached 0.94 recall at a workload reduction of 61 percent. We describe the prompt design, the batching scheme, and a human adjudication step for borderline records.

title: LLMs for title/abstract screening in systematic reviews: a benchmarking study
abstract: This benchmarking study compares several large language models on the abstract screening task using four reference reviews. Recall of 0.94 is reported together with a 61 percent reduction in manual screening effort. Prompt design and a borderline adjudication workflow are documented.

title: Automated data extraction from clinical trial reports using GPT-4
abstract: A structured extraction pipeline reads randomized-trial reports and returns population, intervention, and outcome fields with a verbatim evidence span for each. On a held-out set the field-level accuracy was 0.88, with the remaining fields routed to a human review queue rather than accepted silently.

title: Data extraction from trial reports with GPT-4: accuracy and error analysis
abstract: We analyse the errors of an automated data-extraction pipeline applied to randomized-trial reports. Field-level accuracy reached 0.88; a taxonomy of the residual errors is presented, and every unverifiable value is queued for a human rather than accepted.

title: Automated Screening of Abstracts Using Large Language Models
abstract: This preprint reports an abstract-screening system built on an instruction-tuned language model. We measure recall, workload savings, and calibration of the model's own confidence scores across three review topics.

title: Automated screening of abstracts using large language models (extended)
abstract: This extended version of an earlier preprint reports an abstract-screening system built on an instruction-tuned language model, adding a fourth review topic and an analysis of confidence-score calibration and of workload savings.

title: Deduplication of bibliographic records with embedding similarity
abstract: Exact identifier matching misses a large share of duplicate records that arise when the same study is indexed by several databases with divergent metadata. We show that sentence-embedding similarity over title and abstract recovers most of these near-duplicates while keeping false merges below one percent.

title: A rapid review workflow combining machine learning and human screening
abstract: We describe a rapid-review workflow in which a machine-learning classifier ranks records by predicted relevance and reviewers screen from the top until a stopping criterion is met. The approach cut calendar time by half on two commissioned reviews without missing any included study.

title: Topic modelling of nursing research abstracts with BERTopic
abstract: BERTopic is applied to twelve thousand nursing-research abstracts to describe the thematic structure of the field over a decade. The paper is a substantive application rather than a methods contribution, though it discusses parameter choices in some detail.

title: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation for evidence synthesis
abstract: We test whether retrieval-augmented generation can draft accurate evidence summaries from a set of included studies. Grounding every sentence in a retrieved passage reduced unsupported claims sharply, but roughly one summary in six still required substantive correction by a methodologist.

title: Reporting guidance for AI-assisted systematic reviews
abstract: This article proposes an extension to existing reporting guidelines covering how automated and AI-assisted steps of a review should be documented, including model identifiers, prompt versions, and the human oversight applied at each stage.

title: Citation chasing tools: a comparative study
abstract: Four backward- and forward-citation tools are compared on their ability to surface studies missed by a database search. Yield varied widely by discipline; the tools are positioned as a supplement to, not a replacement for, a structured search.

title: Patient perspectives on shared decision making in oncology
abstract: A qualitative interview study of thirty patients receiving cancer treatment, exploring how they experience shared decision making with their care team. No computational or review-automation component is involved.

title: A randomized trial of a mobile app for smoking cessation
abstract: Eight hundred adult smokers were randomized to a smartphone application or usual care. Biochemically verified abstinence at six months was the primary outcome. This is a primary intervention study.

title: Editorial: why we still need human reviewers
abstract: A first-person editorial arguing that enthusiasm for automating systematic reviews has outrun the evidence. It offers opinion and anecdote; it presents no method and no data.

title: Machine translation quality for low-resource languages
abstract: A benchmark of neural machine-translation systems on eight low-resource language pairs. The work concerns translation quality in general and is not about literature reviews or their automation.

title: Trial registry data mining for outcome reporting bias
abstract: An automated pipeline compares registered and published outcomes across twelve thousand trials to quantify outcome reporting bias. The automation targets primary trial records, not the literature-review process.

title: Blockchain for supply chain provenance
abstract: A design study of a distributed ledger for tracking goods through a manufacturing supply chain. Entirely unrelated to evidence synthesis or review automation; included here only as a clear-exclude control.
